story_type: army engineers' demolition training ends in a record blast
hook: The biggest blast this Army base had seen in over a decade.
narration: This Army base had not seen a blast like this in more than ten years.
Combat engineers at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, spent days training with real demolitions.
Day two was doors. They taped bags of water onto a charge to punch through heavy metal.
The finale used shaped charges, fifteen pounds of explosive each.
A shaped charge has a hollow cone inside that focuses the blast into a jet, so it can drill a deep hole for a bigger charge.
The goal was a crater so big that an Abrams tank could not drive through it.
[short pause] Then everyone pulled back, and the field went quiet.
outcome: The shaped and cratering charges made the biggest explosion on that base in over a decade.
title: Biggest blast on an Army base in 10 years
description:
Combat engineers with the 23rd Brigade Engineer Battalion, 7th Infantry Division, ran heavy demolition training at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, on Sept. 13, 2023. Their shaped and cratering charges produced the biggest explosion on the base in over a decade.

Footage: U.S. Army video by Pfc. Elijah Magana, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/897670/biggest-explosion-jblm-over-decade
